items.title: The Hunting Wives Recap: An Act of Margo Banks
items.description: That Lincoln Trout is no good! We are treated to a flashback from eight months ago, where we learn just how far he is willing to go for this job. He lures the other candidate for the Jed Banks gig back to his hotel room, before tying him up and leaving him to
items.author: Christina Grace Tucker
paragraphs: That Lincoln Trout is no good! We are treated to a flashback from eight months ago, where we learn just how far he is willing to go for this job. He lures the other candidate for the Jed Banks gig back to his hotel room, before tying him up and leaving him to choke on the sock that Lincoln stuffed in his mouth. Lincoln swoops into his job interview and manages to convince the man in charge that he is right for this. Yeah, this is definitely the guy who hired a 24/7 killer/bodyguard for Margo. Bad sign!

Sophie is desperate for info and desperate to talk to Margo. So desperate, in fact, that she comes knocking on Nadia’s door. Callie answers and tells Sophie they are filming confessionals tomorrow, but that’s all. Despite Sophie’s many pleas for more information, Callie hits her with a “best of luck,” and a door closes in her face. Devastating! But iconic!

C&N Private Eye is far too busy cracking this case to worry about SOPHIE, please. When Callie comes back, Nadia has just gotten off the phone, linking another piece of evidence, this time the gun used to kill Abby, to Kyle, Margo’s brother. Nadia is ready to confront Margo TOMORROW at the confessional shoot, but Callie needs to think. She had feelings for Margo once — can she really condemn a woman she cared about to the clink?

Jail might sound good to Margo right now, actually! She’s in a different kind of jail, one where all she is allowed to do is go to campaign events and hang out in the house. They won’t even let her have a phone, but she is Margo fucking Banks after all, and gets around that by setting up a hair appointment in her name under Sophie’s number. When the salon calls to confirm, Sophie knows where to go. Their plan works, and Sophie is even able to smuggle Margo a burner phone. Damn, when push comes to shove, Sophie locks the fuck in, huh? But how the hell are they going to get Margo out of this? Jed is the problem, so they need leverage on Jed. Sophie’s eyes light up, and she has a solution. She’ll give Old Eye Patch a call and buy his file of Jed blackmail material! Brilliant thinking! She sets up a meeting, but someone has already beaten her to it. Goddamn it!

After getting pressure from Callie and Wanda, Jonny finally comes to the Banks’ with the news of Kyle’s death. He wants to confirm this terrible news with DNA, and even though Margo is boo-hooing with the best of them, Jonny doesn’t seem to be buying it. Jed doesn’t NEED this right now, damn it, but for the first time, Johnny throws his weight around. He’s got a man shot thanks to all this mess, so he’d like to figure out what’s going on. Margo uses this time to duck into the bathroom to call Sophie. The dangerous duo is panicked, especially when Sophie admits she didn’t get anything out of the eyepatch man. Margo is the one who realizes that Jai-Yi must have gotten to them after she got sacked by Lincoln Trout. Thankfully, Jai-Yi’s love for midday cardio is no match for Sophie’s love of stalking, and Sophie manages to get her to agree to a deal. One million dollars, split between Sophie and Jai-Yi. Of course, Jai-Yi immediately goes home and calls Lincoln Trout, ready to flip for higher pay. Oh girl, I fear you might be making the highest payment there is, with this one.

Callie is still not sure what to do about Margo, so she heads to see the Reverend in the hospital to talk about faith and guidance. The Rev is quite disillusioned at this point with the whole thing. I mean, I get it, but you know, sir, you could have tried one time to get your son real tangible help? The fact that he will have the bullet his son shot him with lodged in his chest for the rest of his life is kind of a bummer; I get that. He’s having a real crisis of faith, but it’s helping Callie realize something. None of this was an act of God or a divine punishment. This was an act of Margo Banks.

The wool is gone from Callie’s eyes, and she heads back to the hotel, ready to put Margo in the slammer. Nadia wants one piece of evidence they can startle her with, one bit of proof she can’t deny. Luckily, Callie has just the thing: photos of Margo and Brad on the very night of the murder. She confesses she took them while lurking in the bushes like a stalker, and it’s clear that she’s worried Nadia is gonna be like “see you later you absolute FREAK,” but Nadia warps her in a hug instead. I am rooting for these two, sue me!!!

Callie and Nadia welcome Margo to the confessional shoot like it’s gonna be just the best time ever. And you know what, maybe for them it will be? Nadia softballs her for like one second before leaping to questions Margo refuses to answer, no matter how hard Nadia pushes. So she drops the big one, throwing the photos up on her laptop screen and throwing them in Margo’s face. To credit, Margo doesn’t blink. She tries to say that Callie is a stalker and unwell, but when Nadia doesn’t back down, she folds. Props to Nadia for being the first person to say that Brad was a BOY she was sleeping with! Nadia is really confident and aggressive, talking to a woman who she thinks is a murderer and one we KNOW is a murderer, twice over! Margo uses her early end time to slip out of her shadow’s sight, disappearing into the woods in a shot that did actually make me lol.

Sophie has been tracking Jai-Yi down to see why she blew off their meeting. Once again, she is able to locate her apartment building, and oh my gosh, what does she walk in on but Jai-Yi being KILLED by Lincoln Trout and his security killer! She manages to get the hell outta there by the skin of her teeth, and picks up Margo from the woods somehow? Thankfully, it gives them a moment to catch up. Yeah, Nadia knows everything, from Abby to Brad, and yes, Lincoln is a stone-cold freak and killer. Oh, and there is a car following them! Fun! Thanks to Sophie’s new car, she’s able to pull a move that sends the hulking SUV flipping over them and crashing dramatically on the pavement. Will our intrepid duo pull it off? Could it be that they are free?

• Certain that their John Doe is Kyle Burkett, Wanda gets permission to run down the numbers of the cell phones in the location his truck was found. Sophie comes right on up, but so do three others, and Jonny wants her to run through them all before zeroing in on Sophie.
• Jai-Yi’s response to Sophie asking where the file is. “You think I carry it around in my purse like a fucking tampon?”

items.title: The Hunting Wives Recap: No More Scissor Sisters
items.description: Six months ago: Brad is planning his promposal when Margo drops by. Jill should be back in a minute, but in the meantime, can he practice his promposal dance on her? Crazy of him to choreograph it to “Lose Control” by Teddy Swims. It’s crazier still for this w
items.author: Christina Grace Tucker
paragraphs: Six months ago: Brad is planning his promposal when Margo drops by. Jill should be back in a minute, but in the meantime, can he practice his promposal dance on her? Crazy of him to choreograph it to “Lose Control” by Teddy Swims. It’s crazier still for this whole performance to be working on her? They almost kiss, but Jill returns from the store in the nick of time.

In the present, Margo is trying to gently talk Brad down like he’s a spooked animal. It works well enough; she gets him to drop the gun and sit with her on the couch. She asks what’s wrong, and the dam breaks. He’s confused about his mother, and this thing his dad said about her not being a killer. He insists there is proof, but Margo reminds him that his mother did kill Starr, and that she was unwell. To say the least of it! She almost has him where she wants him, but Brad’s mind is working now. There were only four people at the lakehouse, and out of all of them, Margo is the only one who had motivation to kill Abby. “Did you care about me at all?” he asks plaintively, before both of their eyes fall on the gun. Margo is the faster draw, and despite Brad begging that he knows how to keep a secret, Margo shoots him. Damn, that is the second teenager she’s murdered. That’s a little nutty, no?

All of this happens mere moments before Sophie arrives, and Margo doesn’t even bother to sugarcoat it. He knew that Margo killed Abby, so she shot him. Sophie locks in. They have to call the cops, and they have to tell Jonny that Brad attacked Margo, so she shot him in self-defense. Sophie gives her a big old shiner to make the story believable, and Jonny buys it. Both because he’s kind of an idiot, but also because Brad killed Chase Brylan, shot his own father, and was on drugs. As far as Jonny is concerned, case closed!

In bed, Sophie is telling Margo that none of this is her fault (all of it is), and Margo is wondering if she is a sociopath. Hmm. I don’t know what you are, babe, but I am a little scared! Sophie insists that if Margo is, so is she. Well … yeah, I could see that. In the morning, Margo is gone, back to Alba to have some memories and a dark day of the soul.

Jed is PISSED to have to leave the campaign trail and deal with Margo and her usual dead body baggage. The fact that she is simply MIA is not helping her case at all! Lincoln Trout is in agreement, and even losing a touch of his trademark cool. “On one hand, voters love her. On the other, she keeps getting wrapped up in fucking murders!” Lincoln Trout wants that lady on a leash ASAP!

When Shopie drops Jack off from school, Graham has had enough. He is pissed upon hearing that she is wrapped up in yet another murder, and he’s not even hearing it from her. “If I had to set a meeting every time a body dropped in your orbit, we’d never get anything done!” You know what? Fair enough! He threatens her with full custody, and Sophie goes kinda Margo on his ass, if I’m being honest? She’s like Oh, you think I hang out with murderers? Go ahead, take my son, see what happens. Girl! This is not a compelling case to keep a child in your custody! Finally, Margo reappears, and the bonkers duo makes plans to meet at the Halloween fair.

Nadia goes to see Callie and explain herself. Starr was the one who called the network, like literally seconds before she died, and Nadia used that to get a deal with the network. Three months to crack the case, a budget, and clearance for a fake show. Damn, how much money does the Christian Network have? Probably troubling to discover the real answer, huh? Callie demands to know who really killed Abby, if everything they know is a lie. Nadia admits she doesn’t know, and Callie throws her to curb again … but it does kick her mind into gear. She bugs Jonny for more information, and finally comes back to Nadia, who properly apologizes for lying and manipulating, while also fully admitting that’s part of the job and a part of her personality. Callie wants proof that Nadia cares about her more than the show, and just when I start to think that Callie has gone too hard, Nadia goes harder. She sits down and whips up an email that says she resigns from her job and the show effective immediately, because she fell in love with the star. LOVE! Awwww, God bless lesbians, never change, my people! Callie stops her from sending the email because she’s not a fucking idiot, and even though she loves her man, she is aware that he might have fumbled the bag here. She wants everything Nadia has on this murder, now. The two of them put the motives and people in place REALLY damn fast, and by the time the scene ends, the two of them are sure Margo killed Abby. Bad news for Margo!

At the Halloween fair, the vibes are bad, immediately. Lincoln Trout calls Sophie on her way there, casually informing her that she will never see Margo again, and if she tries, Jack very well might go missing. Oh fun! She calls Margo to tell her about this new wrinkle in their lives, but Margo is about to find out what her new life looks like. A giant man grabs her at the fair and escorts her to Lincoln, who tells her there is a new world order: his. No more fun and games on this campaign trail; she is under 24/7 supervision, and her bodyguard, Kane, seems very comfortable with breaking fingers. This is all told to Margo seconds before she joins Jed on stage, and in the crowd, she and Sophie look at one another, two sets of big blue eyes quivering with tears and lesbian longing. Yikes!

• Margo’s trailer-induced flashback involves a teenage Margo begging her mother to wake up and help her sew a thrifted prom dress. Her mother comes to enough to help, but the mother-daughter bonding time is interrupted by a young Zelda, looking for money. She pistol-whips Margo’s mom, then takes Margo’s money, imparting some wisdom to a young, impressionable Margo. “She eats what she hunts; you eat what you hunt.” It’s a dog-eat-dog world, girlie — welcome to it!

• Jamie, so nice to see you again! I wish it were not because your best friend was killed, and I wish you were not sobbing in a server alley about it. Nadia comes to get information about the lake house night, but Jamie isn’t about to talk about it at work. They agree to meet at a hotel, but not before Jamie stops by Sophie’s place to give her a heads up. No matter how much stammering and panicking she does, this boy is not moved. He’s right! Sadly, the odds for teenagers on this show are really bad! Stay alive at all costs, Jamie! Not a great sign that Sophie ends up reporting this to Jed, is it?
• Love the little moment when Chet and Jonny agree on the hat. Rock those hats, boys!

items.title: The Hunting Wives Recap: Good Evening, Ms. Banks
items.description: While I admit I have been a little annoyed at the many moving pieces and timelines of this second season, I do have to admit it is all rather tidy and all stems from one event: Margo sleeping with Brad. Abby’s murder, Sophie getting caught up in it, Sophie kil
items.author: Christina Grace Tucker
paragraphs: While I admit I have been a little annoyed at the many moving pieces and timelines of this second season, I do have to admit it is all rather tidy and all stems from one event: Margo sleeping with Brad. Abby’s murder, Sophie getting caught up in it, Sophie killing Kyle, Nadia’s involvement — none of it would have happened if Margo had not, you know, raped a teenager. So it makes sense that this episode culminates with Brad waiting for Margo in her house with a gun, doesn’t it? But it takes us a minute to get there, so here we go!

It’s a good night to get down to business in Maple Brook! Sophie and Margo are enjoying their newfound domestic bliss, Jonny and Chet are keeping it #professional by fucking at work, and Callie is strapping Nadia down, my actual word! My girl is a born top, I’ll tell you what! It’s also nice to see her with someone who actually likes her, as Nadia clearly does. She confirms that they are dating, and it’s very sweet to see Callie all giggles and stars in her eyes. We all know the show is about the Abby Jackson murder, and boy, I am not looking forward to Callie finding out! But there is no time for that, cause Nadia has to run and meet up with Chet in the park for some light blackmail. Look, if you are gonna fuck the sheriff in his office, perhaps turn off the mics?

Chet has the missing piece Nadia has been searching for. She’s never bought the theory that Jill killed Abby, so getting traffic cam photos of Jill on her way home ten minutes before the murder has her feeling quite good. I imagine the orgasms also didn’t hurt. Chet seems kind of hilariously (and troublingly?) unconcerned about this huge piece of evidence that went missing? The case is CLOSED, and that’s all he has to say about that! Nadia just rolls her eyes before confirming he is gonna stay on her blackmail list until this is all sorted out. For now, she’s gotta get to the Married Justice photoshoot, where she picks out a sexy blazer for her new gf. Said GF is feeling a little nervous to see Margo, as Callie hasn’t seen her since she drove over to call her a cunt. But the two of them manage to have a bonding moment about their new significant others, and it seems all signs are pointing towards a renewed friendship.

After the photo shoot, Nadia takes Callie to see the proofs, bragging about how hot and cool she is. “He protects … but she serves.” They celebrate by making out, but before they can get to the good stuff, Nadia’s phone rings. She steps out, and Callie uses her moment of privacy to click on the VERY prominent and very tempting item “MARRIED JUSTICE SIZZLE.” Of course, it’s all about Abby’s murder, and ugh, my heart hurts for poor Callie! Can one person just tell her the truth, please? Nadia insists that she never meant to hurt Callie; she’s desperate to explain, but Callie wants her out, and I think that’s fair. Nadia, how else did you think this was gonna go?

Meanwhile, our two murderers are just as happy as can be, taking giant baths in Margo’s house while Jed is out campaigning. Sophie has decided she doesn’t mind Jed and Margo’s relationship, as long as Margo isn’t fucking other women; she’s as happy as can be. Kind of a wild turnaround from “your husband is a creep who wants to fuck me,” but Sophie is not known for making smart choices, now is she? In tougher news, Graham is not being cool about their divorce; in fact, he has repossessed the Tesla, and now Sophie is stranded with a Halloween costume in one hand and no car to drive. One little call to her girlfriend later, and she’s at the dealership. Sophie mostly needs to pick up her son and go to the grocery store, but before you know it, Margo has her in a gorgeous little green sports car. Shoutout to Porsche for the sponsorship; I hope you were listening to all the details about the car! But if it takes Porsche money to get a better wig on Malin Ackerman, well, it was all worth it! Also, Margo reallllly wants Sophie to come to church with her, and because she is #downbad, Sophie agrees.

And finally, we have Brad. He’s gone from hanging with Chase at parties and photoshoots to doing a guided ayahuasca trip, and I hope you are ready, because it’s quite a trip! After ingesting (and then throwing up) the drugs, he “wakes up” in his house, set to “Crazy.” Jill is there to welcome him, but it turns nasty very quickly. One moment she is talking about how much she loves him, and the next she is calling every other woman in his life a whore. Finally, she insists that he have a snack, unbuttoning her blouse so he can breastfeed. Brad tries to push her away, and she tells him that she gave him “everything he ever wanted.” Brad screams that he didn’t want it, and there is our confirmation that Jill sexually abused him. This is a logical place to take this storyline, and season one laid enough groundwork for it to feel earned. And though this show tends to trend toward “silly and on the nose,” this storyline has been pretty well handled. It is clear that Brad is not well, and his mother’s actions are clearly being condemned, not used for titillation. My problem is that the show treats his relationship with Margo like a sexy secret instead of a straight-up crime! You can’t have it both ways!

Deep in his hallucination, Brad kills his mother, and then immediately comes to the real world to discover that he has, in fact, killed Chase Brylan. Pants around his ankles, so we can guess that the combination of real-life attempted assault and memories of abuse led the boy to snap. R.I.P. John Stamos, and just wondering, player to player, what was your day rate for this? Worth it??

The next morning at church, everyone is just holding on for dear life. Callie is fighting back tears as the girls ask her about the photoshoot and the show; Nadia is trying to talk to the Reverend about the fact that his wife was not a killer, but he doesn’t want to hear it. He gets maybe three sentences in for the sermon before Brad appears, in a hospital gown and jeans. Brad begs his father for help, and the Reverend promptly ends services for the day. Maybe the first time in his life he put his kid before work, but does it count if he’s only doing it because his kid embarrassed him at work? I submit it does not! Also, Brad has a gun! It doesn’t really matter, but I am curious about how Brad got from Austin back to Maple Brook and also saw a doctor and grabbed a gun? Busy kid! The Reverend tries to talk him down, even telling him that his mother did not kill Abby, but it’s too late for Brad. When the Austin PD calls, Brad knows the jig is up. He begs his father not to answer the phone, but his father clearly doesn’t believe his son is a killer and picks up. Brad shoots him, then leaves.
Margo and Sophie are planning another grand night of romance, but instead, Margo comes home to Brad and gun in her living room. Ruh-roh!

• HUGE development for Wanda and Walter: they slept together! Weeks ago, right before Wanda came back from her injury. In the flashback, we can tell Walter is clearly hoping for a relationship, but Wanda doesn’t want it to get messy since they work together. In the present, at Walter’s bedside, Wanda thinks she might have made a mistake. “What is the point in caring if you don’t have anyone to care about?” Good point, my friend!

• Jonny has, of course, assigned the John Doe case to Wanda, and she is intrepidly digging into it, as she is wont to do. Dr. Bob in the morgue senses something is off with her, and her many lingering glances at Walter’s desk make me think she is missing her buddy! John Doe has been nibbled on by too many creatures to make an ID, so she’ll just have to rely on the bag of items on the body. Her one stroke of luck? The set of keys that she finds. They turn on the truck that she has been insisting is Kyle’s, and with this one piece of evidence, she might have figured out the whole Kyle Burkett mess. Can I get a “hell yea, Wanda?”

items.title: Box Office: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Leads With $15 Million on Thanksgiving Eve, ‘Focker In-Law’ Earns $5 Million on Opening Day
items.description: “Sunrise on the Reaping” stuffed the box office competition ahead of Thanksgiving, generating $15 million on Wednesday. Fueled by positive word-of-mouth, Lionsgate’s “Hunger Games” prequel looks to collect $85 million over the five-day holiday period, which wo
items.author: Rebecca Rubin
paragraphs: “Sunrise on the Reaping” stuffed the box office competition ahead of Thanksgiving, generating $15 million on Wednesday. Fueled by positive word-of-mouth, Lionsgate’s “Hunger Games” prequel looks to collect $85 million over the five-day holiday period, which would push its domestic tally to $233 million.

Despite opening last weekend, “Sunrise on the Reaping” towering over two new releases. Disney’s animated “Hexed” earned $7.6 million from 3,725 theaters, and Universal’s comedy “Focker In-Law” grossed $5.3 million from 3,382 venues on their respective opening days. (“Focker In-Law” didn’t have Tuesday previews; showtimes began on Wednesday.) Although “Hexed” has pulled ahead on Wednesday charts, the fantasy adventure is projected to finish the weekend in third place behind “Focker In-Law.” Based on updated projections, “Hexed” is now targeting a five-day debut of $31 million to $35 million, while “Focker In-Law” is aiming for $35 million to $36 million over the same frame. Both films are falling short of pre-release expectations, which forecasted a $40 million to $45 million haul.

Elsewhere, Netflix’s Brad Pitt-led “The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” brought in $910,00 from 252 Imax screens on Wednesday. The sequel to Sony’s “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,” which isn’t getting a traditional wide release, is expected to earn $4 million to $5 million by Sunday.

In the case of “Hexed,” this opening weekend could spell trouble. That’s because the studio spent more than $200 million to produce the film, and theaters keep about half of ticket sales. So the studio needs the movie to resonate in international markets, and throughout holiday season, to justify the sizable prize tag.

Disney has long dominated the Thanksgiving corridor, and the studio’s animated sequels, namely “Moana 2” and “Zootopia 2,” are some of the holiday’s biggest earners of all time. Post-pandemic, however, Disney has struggled with original offerings, including 2024’s “Wish” ($31 million over its first five days) and 2022’s “Strange World” ($18 million debut over its first five days). “Wish” tapped out with $254 million worldwide on a $200 million budget, while “Strange World” left theaters with $73 million globally on a $180 million budget. What’s promising in this case, though, is that audiences seem to like “Hexed,” which was awarded an “A-” grade on CinemaScore exit polls. Positive sentiment should help the film’s box office longevity. The story follows a teen girl who discovers magical powers that take her from suburbia to Hexe, the world of witches.

“Focker In-Law” also carries a sizable budget; Universal and Paramount co-financed the film for $90 million. Although theatrical comedies have become a box office rarity, the three prior “Focker” movies were notable box office winners. The original comedy of errors, 2000’s “Meet the Parents,” starring Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro as mismatched in-laws Greg Focker and Jack Byrnes, generated $330 million worldwide. The 2004 sequel “Meet the Fockers” is the highest-grossing in the franchise with $522 million worldwide, while 2010’s “Little Fockers” amassed $310 million worldwide. In this installment, Ariana Grande joins in the festivities the girlfriend of Greg’s son Henry (Skyler Gisondo) who meets the family as they gather for Jack’s 80th birthday party. Critics panned the film (a 29% on Rotten Tomatoes) but moviegoers have been more receptive; “Focker In-Law” holds a “B+” grade on CinemaScore exit polls.

Despite the range of offerings, this Thanksgiving will fall short of cementing any box office records. Ticket sales are expected to hit $210 million to $215 million across all films in the marketplace. Thanksgiving 2024 was the holiday’s biggest on record with $422 million across all films, led by “Moana 2″ ($225 million debut), “Wicked” ($118 million) and “Gladiator II” ($44 million). Last year was among the top five with $293 million, boosted by “Zootopia 2” and “Wicked: For Good.” Theater owners aren’t discouraged because domestic ticket sales are already 20% above the same point in 2025. Plus, North American revenues are projected to surpass $10 billion for the first time since Covid upended the theatrical business.

items.title: Record Store Day Co-Founder on How Black Friday Evolved Into a Major Holiday for Vinyl Hounds, and What Will Fly Off the Shelves This Year
items.description: In April of this year, the 19th installment of Record Store Day was the event’s most successful ever, but Nov. 27 brings another opportunity for music junkies to get their vinyl on: Record Store Day Black Friday.
items.author: Andrea Dresdale
paragraphs: In April of this year, the 19th installment of Record Store Day was the event’s most successful ever, but Nov. 27 brings another opportunity for music junkies to get their vinyl on: Record Store Day Black Friday.

While the O.G. Record Store Day was conceived as a general celebration of independent record stores, and features limited-edition, in-store only releases, the Black Friday edition exists for a different reason: to give those indie stores a slice of the “biggest shopping day of the year” pie. That’s also why the vinyl releases you’ll find making their debuts on Black Friday are more likely to remain there for the rest of the holiday season, and why many stores will make them available on their websites starting on Saturday the 28th.

The concept of hyping local independent record stores as a must for holiday shopping may sound rather obvious, but RSD co-founder Michael Kurtz says that, at first, he was opposed to the idea, which his wife came up with.

“I was not on board with it,” he admits. “My initial response at the time was, ‘Ah, that’s for big-box stores and selling cheap toasters and stuff.’” But eventually, he came around, thinking they could do “a little bit smaller version” for the holidays. RSD Black Friday does feature fewer releases overall, but its main goal is to get customers through the door. “Most record stores do about two months’ worth of business” that day, Kurtz says.

For Black Friday, Kurtz says what you’ll find in the racks is largely thanks to what he calls a “Secret Squirrel group” of about 20 record store owners nationwide, who help winnow down the overwhelming numbers of releases pitched by artists and record labels.

“They’ve been around forever; they run iconic record stores,” Kurtz explains of this crate-digging cabal. “And I go to them and say, ‘Hey, do you think record stores would want to have this?’ Because Black Friday is not the same as Record Store Day. It’s not supposed to be just a limited thing only. It’s also supposed to be things that record stores want to have in their bins year-round.”

But what’s true for both events is that they feature releases from a dizzying array of artists across multiple genres. That big tent approach, Kurtz reveals, was inspired by Metallica bassist Robert Trujillo, who early on convinced Kurtz to do a vinyl release by iconic jazz bassist Jaco Pastorius.
“It went to No. 1 on Billboard‘s jazz chart,” Kurtz recalls. “And that made us rethink: ‘Oh, geez, we could do jazz records, we could do bluegrass records, we could do soul records, R&B, funk.”

Of course, rock in its various forms is still a huge focus of both Record Store Day and RSD Black Friday, but in recent years, pop artists have climbed on board the vinyl train en masse, resulting in a surprising boom in customers who are too young to even remember a world where vinyl was once the only option.

Kurtz says, “The majority of people who come to Record Store Day now and participate are younger than the age of 35, and slightly more female than male.” Of course, you can credit the biggest pop star in the world for that.

While Kurtz says Billie Eilish’s 7-inch releases for RSD “sort of cracked the door open” for that demographic, he notes, “It got blown wide open with Taylor Swift. When she did her ‘Long Pond Studio Sessions’ record with us exclusively for record stores [in 2023], it changed everything.” That album became the first Record Store Day exclusive release ever to hit the top 10 of theBillboard200, proving that brand-new releases on vinyl could do just as well as streaming titles.

For RSD Black Friday 2026, Kurtz predicts that it’ll be Noah Kahan’s vinyls getting the youth through the door. “He’s got a special 7-inch that was done just for record stores that’s very very cool: It’s tied in with the ‘Hunger Games’ soundtrack,” says Kurtz, referring to “Draw You Out,” Kahan’s contribution to “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping – The Album.” “And then he’s also got an additional record that’ll be highly sought after.” That would be “The Last of the Bugs,” which collects the four tracks Kahan added to the expanded edition of his album”The Great Divide.”

Kurtz is also excited about a Bruce Springsteen live box set, the American version of The Beatles’ Rubber Soul LP on gold vinyl, a live album by Billy Joel, a disc of the Doors’ studio sessions and a 2-LP set by Ween “for all the pot smokers out there.”

He also predicts the Miles Davis, Jerry Garcia Band and Grateful Dead releases will be popular, as well as the original, previously unreleased version of Joan Jett’s “I Love Rock & Roll” album and not one but three albums by Japanese guitar virtuoso Masayoshi Takanaka.
Kurtz says he doesn’t even mind that many of those younger customers are buying vinyl not to play, but to display.

“Y’know, I was originally freaked out about that because I’m a music person, but I kind of get it,” he tells me. “Like, I will get the Beatles’ ‘Rubber Soul’ reissue this year and I probably will never open it. I just want it because it’s so beautiful, and to know that I have one of 15,000 copies that will ever be printed … I want to keep it pristine.”

Despite admitting to being “completely anxiety-ridden” each year over how successful each Record Store Day event will be, Kurtz is looking forward to the event’s 20th anniversary next year. He and co-founder Carrie Colliton would love to mark the milestone with live performances and some kind of art installation featuring past Record Store Day releases. (A copy of each of those limited releases is currently stored in a warehouse in Raleigh, North Carolina, in case you might want to pull off the vinyl equivalent of robbing Fort Knox.) But for right now, Kurtz notes, those plans are “dreams right now. They’re not reality.”

Still, the failure he fears is unlikely. Nearly 20 years into an event which has helped drive pop culture back to the vinyl age, Kurtz says there’s no sign of its popularity tapering off. As he notes, “demand for [vinyl] and the excitement around it is completely still there – even more so, I think.” But, he acknowledges, “The only thing that’s a bit alarming is how expensive it’s becoming” – a reflection of the rising cost of shipping due to increases in gas and diesel.

“It’s stunning for me as a person who’s ridden this tiger called Record Store Day for almost 20 years to see it from the beginning: When we first started we were the only ones doing new vinyl, and in the used bins you could find [high quality copies of] Led Zeppelin or the Beatles or Pink Floyd for $3, $5 — those days are over.”

Kurtz says it was interesting working with shops in the early days, and still can be today — because they’re independent in all sorts of ways, including what they prefer to emphasize in their stores and sometimes think RSD should focus on as a whole.

“The most difficult thing about putting it together was working with record store owners, because they’re a very creative bunch,” he says. “They’re very different; they’re not people who typically play by the rules. They like to do things their way. So to try to get them all together to do this was very difficult.” He adds, “I was in London once and there was a record store owner who just just raked me over the coals because we’d done the Taylor Swift record. I was like, ‘What records do you like?’ He’s like, ‘Yes, Black Sabbath, Deep Purple …’ and I said, ‘OK I get it. That’s what you love and what you’re passionate about, but there’s another generation.’ And so it’s working with them and not alienating them, because sometimes I do that by accident.”

items.title: BBC’s Antisemitism Crisis Represents an Unprecedented Chapter for the World’s Most Trusted News Organization
items.description: It is a dark day for the BBC.
items.author: K J Yossman
paragraphs: It is a dark day for the BBC.

On Thursday, government adviser Lord John Mann announced he is launching an investigation into alleged antisemitism at the broadcaster. It is an unprecedented chapter for the corporation, long held up as one of the most venerable and reliable media institutions in the world.

For those who have been paying attention, however, the move is not surprising following a litany of public missteps dating as far back as 2021, when BBC News misreported an incident in which a group of Jewish students were attacked on a bus in Central London and then doubled down on it, despite eventually acknowledging the reporting lacked accuracy and impartiality.

Later, the broadcaster steadfastly refused to reprimand Gary Lineker, one of its most high-profile sports anchors, as he repeatedly breached its much-touted social media guidelines, which were instituted precisely because of Lineker’s increasingly political Twitter activity. Under the guidelines, high-profile presenters hosting flagship programs are expected to be impartial while the show is on air and for a two-week window before and after. At the time, he called the guidelines “very sensible.”

It was only when last year Lineker reposted an Instagram story about “Zionists” alongside a rat emoji that the BBC finally cut him loose. Even then, rather than a punitive measure, his exit was presented to the public as a mutually agreed decision for the host to leave after the final “Match of the Day” episode aired the following week. The BBC’s press release went on to call him a “defining voice in football coverage” and “thank him for the contribution he has made.”

Critics compared the BBC’s apparently favorable treatment of Lineker to that of former BBC Radio 5 Live broadcaster Danny Baker, who was sacked immediately in 2019 after tweeting an image of a chimpanzee with the caption “Royal baby leaves hospital” just days after Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, gave birth, with the BBC calling it a “serious error of judgment.”

The following month saw yet another incident when the BBC broadcast a little-known rapper’s rant about a former (apparently Jewish) boss, described alternately as a “fucking Zionist” and “bald-headed cunt,” before the crowd was engaged in a chant of “Death to the IDF.” It later emerged that producers had assessed the rapper as “high risk” and yet decided to broadcast his set live.

Even as he embarked on his rant, which BBC chair Samir Shah later acknowledged consisted of “unconscionable antisemitic views,” no one at the broadcaster thought to cut the Glastonbury feed. Shah apologized for the oversight, and the BBC’s director of music, Lorna Clarke, briefly “stepped back” from her duties, although it appears little other action was taken (she has long since returned to her post).

Then, last month, it was revealed that the BBC had reached an out-of-court settlement with one of its top factual producers, Lucie Kon, after she brought a legal claim alleging antisemitic discrimination. Kon, an Emmy and Oscar winner who exec produced “Mr Nobody Against Putin,” had worked for the corporation for 25 years but said that after Oct. 7, when Hamas murdered 1,200 people in Israel and kidnapped 250 more, the atmosphere toward her changed.

The BBC rejected those claims but agreed to pay Kon £400,000 ($520,000) to settle out of court. For health reasons, Kon accepted. By comparison, the average award handed down by courts for race discrimination in the U.K. is £29,532, according to the most recent statistics.

At the same time, the BBC’s reporting on Israel has been an ongoing source of contention. There was the Gaza documentary which failed to tell viewers the narrator was the son of a senior Hamas official, the report speculating Israel had bombed a hospital in Gaza which had actually been hit by a Hamas rocket misfiring and the news story in which an anchor misrepresented a Reuters story, saying the IDF was “targeting … medical teams as well as Arabic speakers” when in fact the medical teams and Arabic speakers were part of the IDF, there to assess patients on the ground.

A leaked internal report last year — the same one that led to BBC boss Tim Davie resigning when it revealed the BBC had doctored one of President Trump’s speeches — noted that BBC Arabic, a part of the corporation’s World Service, had made 215 corrections and clarifications in its reporting of the Israel-Gaza war since 2023, amounting to two a week. At the time, a BBC spokesperson told Variety: “BBC News Arabic strives for the highest standards of journalism across its services.”

(Incidentally, the BBC World Service currently operates in 45 languages, including Arabic, Amharic, English, Hausa, Kirundi, Marathi, Tigrinya, Ukrainian, Urdu and Yoruba. It does not include Hebrew.)
So how did the BBC find itself embroiled in yet another crisis?

Part of the problem stems from the fact that the corporation effectively marks its own homework. While British newspapers are regulated by an independent body, IPSO, the BBC operates the Executive Complaints Unit to investigate grievances about itself.

But there is also a sense that the BBC, even under its new director general Matt Brittin, is not interested in engaging seriously with the issue. Each time there is a public blunder, the BBC will roll out the same playbook: issue a cut-and-paste apology (usually with reluctance), defend its reporting and make a gesture to suggest it has learned a lesson. But the sheer frequency of incidents — only a handful of which even spin out into the public realm — suggests nothing is being learned.

Earlier this month, the corporation’s deputy director-general, Rhodri Talfan Davies, was asked during an on-the-record Q&A session with journalists whether he would support an internal inquiry into antisemitism at the BBC. His response was to deny there was a “deep-rooted issue” or any “institutional discrimination” at the broadcaster. Notably, he didn’t answer the second part of the journalist’s question, namely, if Talfan Davies didn’t think there was antisemitism at the BBC, “Why do you think many of your Jewish employees think there is?”

Even the corporation’s checkbox response to Lord Mann’s announcement on Thursday gives the impression, whether intended or not, that the threat of an investigation into its internal conduct is of little consequence. When approached for comment, a BBC publicist told Variety by email, “We’d also like to direct you to the below statement, that we’ve previously issued,” before copy-and-pasting it underneath.

In his speech announcing the investigation, Lord Mann said he is “not interested in targeting individuals. That would entirely miss the point. I am targeting the institution.” The biggest clue as to the depth of the BBC’s antisemitism problem will be whether the institution even cares.

items.title: Former Disney Boss Bob Iger ‘Got ABC Employee Pregnant’ During Affair, New Book Claims
items.description: Former Disney boss Bob Iger allegedly impregnated an employee in the 1990s, according to an explosive new book, per the New York Times.
items.author: K J Yossman
paragraphs: Former Disney boss Bob Iger allegedly impregnated an employee in the 1990s, according to an explosive new book, per the New York Times.

The newspaper has published an interview with Wall Street Journal reporter Robbie Whelan, the author of a forthcoming and reportedly unflattering biography of the Disney big cheese titled “The House of Mouse.”

According to the NYT, the book documents a consensual extramarital relationship between Iger and an “ABC marketer” that took place in the early 1990s when Iger was head of ABC and resulted in a pregnancy. Whelan reportedly writes that the woman, who was at the time rungs below Iger on the corporate ladder, allegedly “suffered through a traumatic termination procedure.”

Iger’s 18-year-long reign (split across two tenures) as Disney CEO ended in March, when he was replaced by parks boss Josh D’Amaro. Iger is due to attend his final Disney board meeting next week – the same day “The House of Mouse” is published.

Whelan told the Times that neither Iger nor Disney spoke to him for the book but said his publisher, William Morrow, received legal letters from Iger’s lawyer raising concerns about the tome painting a “false and defamatory” picture.
“Their instinct was to bully me,” Whelan told the Times. He said he spoke to other sources, including former Marvel CEO Ike Perlmutter, who has a frosty relationship with Iger.

“A character having an ax to grind — or a motivation is a better way of putting it — just makes him a better character,” Whelan said of his sources’ possible agendas. “It doesn’t make them disqualified.”
Variety has contacted Disney and Iger’s legal representative for comment.

In a statement to the Times, the company said: “Bob Iger is one of the most respected CEOs of his generation” pointing to his “bold creative and strategic decisions” and that he leaves Disney “stronger and more innovative.”

items.title: Gérard Depardieu to Stand Trial for Rape Charges After Failed Appeal
items.description: French actor Gérard Depardieu will face a criminal rape trial after an appeal from his lawyers failed.
items.author: Ellise Shafer
paragraphs: French actor Gérard Depardieu will face a criminal rape trial after an appeal from his lawyers failed.

According to Reuters, on Thursday the Paris Court of Appeal ruled that a trial would go ahead regarding rape charges that stemmed from accusations made by actress Charlotte Arnould in 2018. She alleged that in August of that year, Depardieu raped her twice at his Paris home. He was indicted in December 2020 and has denied any wrongdoing. Last year, his lawyers appealed the prosecutors’ decision for the case to go to trial.
Though the court rejected his appeal, it ruled that Depardieu will only be tried for the first alleged rape, and not the second. If convicted, the 77-year-old could face 15 to 20 years in prison.

The news comes just 10 days after Depardieu’s withdrawal of a separate appeal regarding his conviction last year on sexual assault charges. He was given an 18-month suspended prison sentence for sexually assaulting two women on the set of his 2021 film “Les Volets Verts.”

In a statement to French newspaper Le Monde, he said: “Justice has spoken. I have been found guilty. I accept this and take responsibility for this conviction,” offering his “deep and sincere apologies” to those who “may have suffered as a result.”

Last week, a new complaint alleged further rape and sexual assault allegations against Depardieu during the filming of Guillaume Nicloux’s “Thalasso” in 2018. His lawyers told French radio station RTL that they were unaware of the complaint, which was filed in May 2025, shortly after his first sexual assault trial.

items.title: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Devouring $85M Over Thanksgiving Weekend as ‘Focker-in-Law,’ ‘Hexed’ Launch
items.description: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is claiming the head of the table at the Thanksgiving weekend box office as Focker-in-Law and Hexed enter the arena.
items.author: Ryan Gajewski
paragraphs: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is claiming the head of the table at the Thanksgiving weekend box office as Focker-in-Law and Hexed enter the arena.

Lionsgate’s sixth film in the dystopian Hunger Games franchise screens in 4,018 North American theaters for its sophomore frame, as it grossed around $15.1 million on Wednesday. Director Francis Lawrence’s adaptation of author Suzanne Collins’ 2025 prequel novel is looking at a five-day sum around $85 million to take its domestic cume to roughly $233 million through Sunday. The movie stars Joseph Zada as a young Haymitch Abernathy, played by Woody Harrelson in the first four Jennifer Lawrence-led films.

After opening to the fifth-biggest launch in Lionsgate history last weekend with $119 million domestically and $225 million worldwide, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping has continued its momentum. The $150 million-budgeted film, which earned an A- CinemaScore, grossed $15.98 million domestically on Tuesday to notch the franchise’s biggest first Tuesday, narrowly topping the $15.96 million for 2013’s Catching Fire. Sunrise’s Monday sum of $12.8 million also bested the series’ previous top opening Monday of $12.3 million for Catching Fire.

The East Coast has been impacted by a major storm stretching from the Midwest to the Eastern seaboard, leading the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York to be moved to Saturday for the first postponement in its 100-year history. The inclement weather could slow down moviegoing throughout the weekend, including on Black Friday, which tends to be the biggest day for the box office over the Thanksgiving frame.

Disney released Hexed in 3,725 North American theaters on Wednesday, with the animated fantasy film collecting an estimated $7.6 million on opening day, including $2.1 million in Tuesday previews. Directors Jason Hand and Fawn Veerasunthorn’s movie, which carries a budget north of $200 million, could be heading for a five-day launch around $35 million. This looks to be down a bit from the $45 million opening that the studio had initially been projecting.

Hailee Steinfeld, Rashida Jones and Jodie Foster lead the voice cast for Hexed, which centers on a mother and her teenage daughter grappling with the girl’s magical powers. The studio has been hopeful that it will continue to run throughout the holiday corridor and follow the lead of this year’s original animated features with pleasing performances, including Goat and Hoppers, although other recent originals like Forgotten Island have struggled.

Earning an A- CinemaScore, Hexed holds a 66 percent critics score on Rotten Tomatoes. The Hollywood Reporter critic Angie Han wrote in her review that it offers “more than enough to make for a pleasurably transportive trip to the theater.”

Universal Pictures’ Meet the Parents sequel Focker-in-Law launched in 3,382 North American theaters on Wednesday, grossing $5.3 million on its opening day. Director John Hamburg’s film appears to be in line for a $36.3 million opening over the five-day frame, also a bit below the initial projection in the $45 million range. Ariana Grande joins franchise returnees Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro, as she plays a woman set to marry the son of Stiller’s Greg Focker.

Meet the Parents opened to $28.6 million domestically in 2000 (en route to its $166.2 million domestic cume). Sequel Meet the Fockers launched even bigger with $70.5 million over the five-day Christmas frame in 2004, while 2010’s Little Fockers dropped to $45 million for its five-day opening frame.

Focker-in-Law earned a B+ CinemaScore from audiences and holds a rough 29 percent critical score on Rotten Tomatoes. In his review for THR, critic Frank Scheck wrote that the sequel “feels like the nadir in a series that recycles the same tired jokes in increasingly desperate manner.”

Disney animated features are known for debuting over Thanksgiving, as Moana 2 opened to a massive $225 million over the five-day weekend in 2024 to help that year’s holiday frame set the all-time record with $423 million across all titles. Last year, Zootopia 2 launched on the Wednesday before Thanksgiving and collected $158 million over the five days to help lead the frame to a combined sum of $290 million. The total for this year’s holiday frame is expected to rank below both of those.

In limited release, Netflix launched director David Fincher’s The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth on 252 Imax screens in North America. The Brad Pitt-led follow-up to 2019’s Once Upon a Time in Hollywood appears headed for around $5 million domestically over the five days before it begins streaming Dec. 23.

items.title: Ben Affleck Negotiates With a Duck as Artists Equity Kicks Off Thanksgiving Campaign for Aflac
items.description: Ben Affleck’s Artists Equity and the insurance company Aflac are using Thanksgiving to launch a new installment of their campaign starring the actor and the namesake duck.
items.author: Alex Weprin
paragraphs: Ben Affleck’s Artists Equity and the insurance company Aflac are using Thanksgiving to launch a new installment of their campaign starring the actor and the namesake duck.

The new spot, dubbed “High Stakes,” is set to debut on the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade on NBC Thursday, and will see Affleck serving as a translator between a team of negotiators… and the Aflac Duck.

Artits Equity and Aflac unveiled their campaign in September via a viral marketing effort that saw Affleck vandalizing Aflac billboards. It’s expected to run through next summer, leaning on tentpole events (like, say this week’s parade) to move it along.
Affleck himself frequently directs commercial spots from Artists Equity

“Sure, it’s funny to have Ben Affleck translating for the Aflac Duck. But the idea is rooted in a simple truth,” said Aflac senior VPand CMO Garth Knutson. “Every year, millions of Americans turn to Aflac agents and HR professionals to help them understand their benefits and make informed decisions about their coverage. In this commercial, Ben does it for 60 seconds. They do it every day.”

“As we explored the bond forming between the Aflac Duck and the Affleck Human, it became clear we needed to show audiences that Ben was gaining a deeper understanding of Aflac and its brand icon,” added Brandon Pierce, co-president and ECD of Artists Equity Brand Studio. “And what better way to prove it than through a high-stakes negotiation where Ben could simply and boldly declare, ‘I speak Aflac.’”

items.title: Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Postponed as Storm Descends on Northeast
items.description: In an unprecedented move, the 100th edition of the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City will be postponed until Saturday Nov. 28, Macy’s and NBC announced Wednesday.
items.author: Alex Weprin
paragraphs: In an unprecedented move, the 100th edition of the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City will be postponed until Saturday Nov. 28, Macy’s and NBC announced Wednesday.
The decision comes as a powerful nor’easter storm is bearing down on the northeast, with potential wind gusts north of 60 miles per hour alongside heavy rain.
It’s also a major headache for the broadcast partner NBC, with last year’s parade drawing over 34 million viewers between NBC and Peacock.

The parade is now expected to kick off on the Upper West Side at 8:30 a.m. on Saturday, with the floats, balloons and performers making their way down to Macy’s flagship store on 34th Street. NBC confirmed that it will broadcast the parade Saturday at 8:30 a.m. to all time zones; it will also stream on Peacock.

“Due to the extreme weather conditions, the city of New York, Macy’s and NBC have decided, in the interest of safety for both the participants and spectators, to move the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, Nov. 28,” an NBC spokesperson told The Hollywood Reporter. “More details to follow. In addition, NBC will telecast the 2025 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade tomorrow at 8:30 a.m. in all time zones.”
It’s also a logistical nightmare, with many performance groups and musical artists coming into town for the parade, and which may need to find alternative travel plans.

The parade has never been canceled in its 100 years, though some of the iconic giant balloons have been grounded when there have been high winds. Balloons are supposed to be grounded if wind gusts top 34 miles per hour.
In 1993, a Sonic the Hedgehog balloon was pushed into a lamppost amid high winds, injuring multiple people, and a similar incident occurred in 1997 with a Cat in the Hat balloon.
This year’s postponement is also a first. New York City officials and Macy’s executives are expected to address the postponement later on Wednesday.

items.title: NBC Uses Thanksgiving TV to Kickstart 2028 LA Olympics Marketing Push
items.description: It’s still 2026, but NBC Sports is using a stacked Thanksgiving TV lineup to tee up the 2028 summer Olympics, which will be held in Los Angeles, California.
items.author: Alex Weprin
paragraphs: It’s still 2026, but NBC Sports is using a stacked Thanksgiving TV lineup to tee up the 2028 summer Olympics, which will be held in Los Angeles, California.

The network is debuting a pair of spots on today’s (surprise rebroadcast of last year’s) Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, and they will re-air on the National Dog Show Presented by Purina and in Thursday night’s national NFL game between the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills.

The spots star Olympic track & field gold medalists Sydney Levrone and Rai Benjamin encountering enormous Olympic rings at famous L.A. locations, like in Griffith park overlooking the city, or on the coast at sunset.

“For LA28, the city itself is going to be one of the stars of the Games, and we wanted this creative to capture what it will mean to welcome the Olympics back to the United States,” said Jenny Storms, CMO of NBCUniversal Television & Streaming. “Sydney and Rai have delivered unforgettable moments for Team USA and seeing them discover the Rings in iconic Los Angeles settings is the perfect way to remind America that the Games are coming home. Thanksgiving is annually one of NBCUniversal’s biggest days and an unmatched platform to continue building excitement for the Olympics.”

NBC officially kicked off its 2028 Olympics marketing at the end of the 2026 winter games in Milan-Cortina in a spot featuring actress Kate Hudson and set to the tune of The Mamas & The Papas’ 1966 classic “California Dreamin.’”
The new spots build on that, teeing up what is sure to be aggressive 2027 push ahead of the 2028 games.

items.title: Two Menswear Darlings Just Made the Most Covetable Boots of 2026
items.description: Say you wanted to create the perfect pair of vintage-style military boots. First, you’d need a designer with impeccable taste and encyclopedic knowledge of vintage workwear; then you'd need a bootmaker with the requisite skills to produce it at the highest lev
items.author: Jeremy Freed
paragraphs: Say you wanted to create the perfect pair of vintage-style military boots. First, you’d need a designer with impeccable taste and encyclopedic knowledge of vintage workwear; then you'd need a bootmaker with the requisite skills to produce it at the highest level. If everything went right, the result would be something like the Modèle 1917, a new collaboration between famed Parisian creative director Gauthier Borsarello and renowned Canadian bootmaker Viberg.

In basic terms, the Modèle 1917 is a pair of boots based on the French Army’s 1917 “brodequin,” a design used by soldiers in the trenches of WWI, available in soft brown suede (Mud) and glossy textured black leather (Pavement). But there’s nothing basic about them. The design comes courtesy of Borsarello, a top-tier collector of vintage workwear and the creative mind behind Gersaint Paris and L’Etiquette magazine. Viberg, a third-generation, family-owned boot specialist, got its start making footwear for forestry crews in British Columbia, and it still builds every pair in its Vancouver Island workshop. While it doesn’t make boots for smokejumpers and loggers anymore, old-school shoemaking techniques like a channeled insole Goodyear welt and stitchdown construction ensure their footwear retains its heirloom-level durability.

The backstory of the “brodequin” begins with the Mdl. 1893, a hobnail-soled marching boot created for French infantrymen in the late 1800s that remained in use until the 1950s. In the First World War, the brodequin’s iron-studded soles and sturdy uppers proved ideally suited to the muddy conditions of the trenches, and American troops soon adopted them in place of their inferior M1904 Marching Shoes. “To me, it’s the blueprint for many combat boots across different countries after WWI,” says Borsarello. “I love the idea that France inspired others after fighting side by side in the trenches. They’re very simple, yet instantly recognizable at the same time.”

For all of its strengths in the field, the original brodequin—whose nickname pays tongue-in-cheek homage to a medieval torture device—wasn’t what you’d call a comfortable boot, especially by modern standards. “They were so stiff that they were almost impossible to walk in,” Borsarello admits. This created something of a design challenge.

To stay as true as possible to the original, Borsarello and Viberg designed the boots on a period-correct “pied haricot” (bean-shaped) last, with a cotton twill lining, solid brass hardware, and reinforced panels that support the midfoot so the forefoot can move freely. To make the Modèle M1917 something you’d actually want to wear, they replaced the hobnailed soles with rubber ones and swapped the original roughout leather for supple American-tanned Horween. The result is a pair of boots that are as comfortable as they are durable, not to mention surprisingly versatile. In other words, exactly what you’d expect from a meeting of these formidable talents.

items.title: Jensen Huang Traded His Leather Jacket for a Humble Cotton Zip-Up During His Nvidia Return
items.description: Jensen Huang is back in. The leather jackets? They’re out. The disgraced former Nvidia CEO reclaimed the top job at the American tech giant yesterday, returning to a big welcome from employees and even the president himself. (Trump told CNBC that he “made the
items.author: Tyler Chin
paragraphs: Jensen Huang is back in. The leather jackets? They’re out. The disgraced former Nvidia CEO reclaimed the top job at the American tech giant yesterday, returning to a big welcome from employees and even the president himself. (Trump told CNBC that he “made the deal” to get Huang back in as CEO.) But as Huang returned to the office where he became a billionaire, something was noticeably different. His gray hair remained neatly side-parted as ever, but his usual standout outerwear was swapped for something a whole lot humbler: a navy cotton jacket.

Or, sort of humbler, anyway. Subtle as it may be, Huang’s zip-up appears to nonetheless hail from luxury designer Dior. (The label did not immediately respond to a request for confirmation or comment.) The $3,300 number is the brand’s zippered shirt, one that he’s actually worn in the past, notably when he landed at Gimpo International Airport in Seoul in June of this year. (That was the same trip during which he got memed for wearing a leather jacket on one of the city’s sweatiest summer days.)

The 63-year-old, who cofounded Nvidia in 1993, wore high-end black leather jackets as his daily uniform for over a decade. In September, he told CBS News he owned between 30 to 40, from brands like Tom Ford, Burberry, Dior, and Dunhill. At a Stanford economic summit in 2024, Huang offered up a very practical, Silicon Valley-esque reason for his leather preference: They don’t make him itch. But they also felt like an intentional effort to use fashion to break beyond the tech industry’s traditionally geeky image, à la Mark Zuckerberg sitting front row at Prada or Adam Mosseri showing up at the Met Gala in Kartik Research.

Following the revelation of his extramarital affairs, however—most notably with an alleged Chinese spy, as well as with at least two Nvidia employees—the garments took on a new meaning. Rather than evoking the likes of James Dean or Marlon Brando, the lush outerwear instead began to suggest a man in the throes of a midlife crisis.

Huang’s return as CEO isn’t unprecedented. For example, OpenAI’s Sam Altman was reinstated after employees revolted against the board’s initial firing of the CEO. The move does, however, raise concerns about national security and Nvidia’s company culture.

The dismissal of the leather jacket marks a new chapter in Huang’s tenure at the helm of Nvidia. It had always been a talking point, and after becoming a symbol of his fall from grace, wearing it again would risk turning it into his own scarlet letter. By swapping out stiff leather for easy, approachable cotton, Huang seems to be signaling the desire for a reset. As he told his staff during his return: “I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around.”

items.title: Thankfully, Omega and Swatch Aren’t Done Making Snoopy MoonSwatches
items.description: Four-plus years into the massive collaboration between Omega and Swatch, the partners are still finding ways to reimagine their blockbuster MoonSwatch. And despite nearly 40 iterations of the piece, they still generate massive excitement. The most recent versi
items.author: Oren Hartov
paragraphs: Four-plus years into the massive collaboration between Omega and Swatch, the partners are still finding ways to reimagine their blockbuster MoonSwatch. And despite nearly 40 iterations of the piece, they still generate massive excitement. The most recent version required interested collectors to fill out an “Electronic Swatch Timepiece Application” in hopes of being selected to purchase one. More than 1.2 million people happily played along. Now, Swatch and Omega are back and playing the hits with a Snoopy-inflected version of the MoonSwatch.

Meet the new Mission to Earthphase - Silver Snowflake. The blacked-out watch is reminiscent of the collector-favorite Speedmaster known as the “Dark Side of the Moon” from 2013. What that watch was lacking compared to this one is an adorable drawing of Snoopy and Woodstock dressed as astronauts and a special silver disc with a unique laser-engraved snowflake design. Safe to say, Omega and Swatch have another hit on their hands.

The black-on-black-on-black design works to great effect here. Everything is rendered in the dark shade: the case, bezel, dial, and matching rubber strap with Velcro closure. Like all MoonSwatch references, the Silver Snowflake model measures 42mm in diameter and features the asymmetric design familiar to Speedy lovers everywhere.

But it’s the easter eggs on the dial that really make this MoonSwatch stand out. Naturally, there are several hidden details. For instance, check out the miniature skis standing in for the indices at 11 o'clock. That’s a special shoutout to the Apollo 11 50th Anniversary of the Speedmaster. This model also returns to a trick employed by the “Cold Moon” MoonSwatch released last November. That watch and this one feature a snowflake design generated at random, meaning each watch is functionally unique. Here, the snowflake appears on a silver-coated disc in the moonphase complication at 2 o’clock.

At 10 o’clock is Swatch and Omega’s signature MoonSwatch “Earth phase” indicator, which bears an image of the Earth with UV ink-coated oceans set against a starry background. Again, look closely: Switzerland is represented in white, its UV ink glowing green in the dark, while Snoopy and Woodstock, represented below, feature secret details in blue-emission UV ink. Protecting the dial is a box-shaped, bio-sourced crystal with an engraved “S” in the center—a detail familiar to fans of vintage Speedmasters, some of which bore “O”-engraved Hesalite crystals.

Like several other MoonSwatch models in the brand’s now-vast collection, buying the Mission to Earthphase - Silver Snowflake requires navigating certain arcane rules. The first part is simple: it’ll be available in stores worldwide this Black Friday, November 27th. However, following that, your only chance to nab one will be when it’s snowing in Switzerland. (And only until March 20th, 2027.) When it comes to the MoonSwatch, simply buying one has become half the fun.

items.title: This Piping Hot Zenith Collaboration Explains the Future of the Watch Market
items.description: This is an edition of the newsletter Box + Papers, Cam Wolf’s weekly deep dive into the world of watches. Sign up here.
items.author: Cam Wolf
paragraphs: This is an edition of the newsletter Box + Papers, Cam Wolf’s weekly deep dive into the world of watches. Sign up here.

In early July, I met with Zenith’s chief product officer Romain Marietta over Zoom to get a sneak peek at a watch that wouldn’t come out until November. The latest Zenith G.F.J., made in partnership with the Los Angeles-based independent watchmaker J.N. Shapiro, is a gorgeous timepiece that combines the former’s mechanical know-how with Shapiro’s meticulously handmade dials. Over four months before the watch was even unveiled to the public, Marietta shared that 20 of the 25 pieces produced had already been sold. Of all the releases from the major Swiss brands in 2026, none better represent the future of luxury watchmaking than this high-end, fussily made, independent-adjacent, sold-out-before-you-ever-heard-about-it G.F.J.

Zenith recently announced that it’s laying off roughly half of its current workforce as it attempts to shift its position in the market. “All of us in our segment, which is described as mid-range, are going through a very difficult period,” Zenith CEO Benoit De Clerck told staff as he explained the restructuring, according to Le Temps. The brand has been shifting upmarket since last year, when it released a rainbow gem-set version of its flagship sport watch. The G.F.J. is the cornerstone of that new business. As the economy tilts even further in favor of the uber-rich, it’s also altering where the bulk of the profits come from for watchmakers. “Wealthy people are still wealthy, and even more wealthy,” Marietta said. “It’s easier [now] to sell high-end watches than watches for 3,000 to 5,000 Swiss francs.”

That’s true. Lorel Monroy, a sales associate at LA’s Feldmar Watch Company, tells me there’s “definitely been an uptick” in interest around Zenith this year. Not for the brand’s flagship Chronomaster, which remains firmly in the starter luxury watch zone at $12,300, but for the far more expensive G.F.J., which starts at $49,900. “The luxury direction is the game changer,” Monroy said. Feldmar only received three G.F.J.s to allocate in 2026 and they were all quickly snapped up. There’s now a waitlist building at the retailer for the upscale model.

When it comes to the G.F.J., Zenith has acted like MacGyver, finding endless uses for its smash-hit model. First released in the spring of 2025, the watch received two very pretty, well-received sequels earlier this year. In March, I got to test out the new onyx-dial version for just a few hours before I had to send it along to Hollywood stylist Fabio Immediato, who promptly strapped it on Simu Liu’s wrist for the Oscars.

Over the summer, Zenith also launched this double-signed program, which allows the brand to work with independent makers like J.N. Shapiro. Before this latest release, the Swiss brand linked up with Japan’s beloved Naoya Hida.

That watch was a fascinating representation of the project—the spotlessly clean dial was straight out of the latter’s workshop. Zenith, a historic brand backed by LVMH, ceded control entirely to the small Japanese indie. It was a massive success. To allocate the pieces, Marietta said they narrowed the list to 10 clients, mainly from the Naoya Hida side, then sent an email that included the price tag of 60,000 Swiss francs but zero images of the watch. “They said yes right away, trusting us with the design,” Marietta said. “And that’s a great testimony of how the trust can be at that level when you buy a piece for [$75,000] without even seeing it, not even a picture.”

One of those clients was Eric Ku, the influential dealer and collector behind online auction platform Loupe This, who has been buying Naoya Hida for years. “There hasn’t been a Zenith release so limited and oversubscribed at the same time in recent memory,” he said. Another buyer was super-collector Eric Peng Cheng, the global CEO of Undefeated, who owns multiple Naoya Hida pieces but had never purchased a modern Zenith directly from the brand until their collaboration with the Japanese maker.

In the topsy-turvy world of watches in 2026, it’s much sexier to be an independent brand than one in the stable of the world’s largest luxury conglomerate. Marietta calls the G.F.J. “an independent brand within our global lineup,” pointing to the high-level finishing and historic movement inside the piece—the type of nerdy details that appeal to the most seasoned collectors driving the industry. “The G.F.J. collection itself is bringing us new clients,” Marietta said. “It's attracting clients who did not really have Zenith on their radar. These guys were more A. Lange & Söhne clients or with independents.”

Zenith created irresistible bait for this new stripe of collectors. The new J.N. Shapiro-designed G.F.J. is absolutely gorgeous. The partners leverage the LA independent’s dedication to creating its dials by hand through a technique known as engine turning. I got to visit Shapiro’s workshop a few years ago and was charmed by the contrast of the brand’s cavernous industrial warehouse and the row of almost medieval-looking engine-turning machines lined up at the front of the room.

The dials of the new collaborative watches were painstakingly made on those very machines—on which a single mistake means tossing the whole thing in the bin—and then shipped off to Switzerland, where Zenith watchmakers installed them into cases. There are three different patterns on the dial, including a basketweave at the center and Shapiro’s signature invention, the Infinity Weave, inside the subdial. Much like on the Naoya Hida version, the dial is all Shapiro. Marietta notes, however, that it already resembles the brick pattern seen on the original G.F.J., which is based on the exterior of Zenith’s manufacture in Le Locle.

Zenith plans to release two collaborative versions of the G.F.J. annually moving forward. According to Marietta, a couple of years down the road, the brand may allow their indie partners to go beyond the dial and play with the case and movement as well.

With the G.F.J., Zenith has created something that is tailor-made for today’s collectors. Seven-figure pieces are currently booming at auction, and it would take Moses himself to part the money flooding into the market right now. These deep-pocketed collectors are most interested in watches from independent makers: Auction houses have sold more million-dollar F.P. Journe watches this year than they have from either Rolex or Patek Philippe. As collectors search for the next hot watchmaker, they’re finding exactly what they’re looking for in a 161-year-old Swiss luxury brand.

items.title: APC Just Dropped a Pair of Incredibly Clean Casios
items.description: We’re in a great era for affordable fashion-collab watches. Timex is leading the way: its link-ups with Noah, Todd Snyder, and J. Crew are masterclasses in adding personality to classic designs without going OTT. But don’t count Casio out of the race. The Japa
items.author: Josiah Gogarty
paragraphs: We’re in a great era for affordable fashion-collab watches. Timex is leading the way: its link-ups with Noah, Todd Snyder, and J. Crew are masterclasses in adding personality to classic designs without going OTT. But don’t count Casio out of the race. The Japanese giant has just followed up its 2024 collab with APC. The pair are perfectly matched: Casio watches are known for being beautifully functional and understated—adjectives that fit APC’s spartan aesthetic too.

The first collaboration between the two brands saw them rework the hallowed A1000 digital-display watch. That release stripped back a lot of the original’s markings and added the APC logo on the dial. This time around, it's the AQ-240 getting a makeover. The case is squarer than the rectangular A1000, and while there’s a narrow window for a digital display, the watch maintains the traditional analog format with hands and hour markers. Here, you get the best of both worlds. The watch is sold out on APC's website but still available through Casio, so act fast if you want one. The silver variant is $110, and the gold goes for $135.

What about the APC-ness of it all? That part is the opposite of loud: as with the previous collab, there isn’t much giving away the brand's participation. We’ve got the APC logo on the dial and the buckle, plus the brand’s guitar-and-dagger insignia engraved out of sight on the caseback. Casio already offers the regular A1000 in a bunch of different colorways, but these two new ones are made specifically for the APC collab. The release includes a silver case with a dark-green dial and another in gold on gold. Both of the pieces have a brushed sun-ray effect on the dial. The vibe is refined and stripped back; this is a fashion watch that almost feels anti-fashion.

Maybe the best way to think about it is as the reverse side of the coin to the excellent new G-Shock 2500 Series. Both come from Casio, and both are minimal and functional. But the G-Shocks are big and bulky, with a design that seems to tip its hat to Patek Philippe’s Nautilus. These new ones are slim and nearly dressy. Put the two new releases together, and you’ve got pretty much all bases covered. And if those aforementioned Timex collabs felt a bit too classicist for you, then the Casio-APC partnership takes things in a more modern direction. Far from just being a cash grab, the “fashion watch” is now one of the best routes into affordable, on-point horology.
This story originally appeared on British GQ.
